title: Toolkit contracts for progressive streamed JSON and deterministic tool handoff
creator: Aisha Menon
description: Goal: Define unambiguous acceptance criteria and developer-facing contracts for streaming structured JSON responses and deterministic tool/function calling behavior. This ticket clarifies scope and decisions for the 'progressive schema' streaming mode, error handling modes, tool handoff guarantees, and developer ergonomics (headers, markers, validation feedback). The output must support: (1) incremental JSON-compatible payloads for low-latency UX, (2) schema versioning and reconciliation signals, (3) deterministic tool invocation semantics with retry/idempotency metadata, and (4) graceful degradation modes when the model emits invalid fragments or a tool endpoint is unavailable. This PRD is scoped to API surface and acceptance tests only; implementation will be handled by ENG with follow-up integration tickets.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming contract includes a single-line JSON preamble header containing: schema_version, message_id (UUID), streaming_mode (full|progressive), and sequence_start_timestamp. Clients must tolerate and parse this header before processing chunks.

Progressive streaming emits well-formed JSON fragments separated by explicit chunk markers: "__chunk_start__" and "__chunk_end__". Each chunk must be either a complete JSON value or a JSON object annotated with "partial": true. Concatenating validated chunks (in order) must reconstruct a valid top-level JSON structure when stream completes.

Schema versioning: server includes schema_version in header and each chunk may carry an optional schema_delta tag. If the client schema does not match, the server must emit a reconciliation hint object ("schema_mismatch": {expected, actual, diff_url}) and not silently change required field types mid-stream.

Chunk validation rules: runtime will validate chunk JSON against the active schema at emission. If a chunk fails validation, server must emit an error-chunk with error_level (soft|hard), error_code, and human_message. Soft errors allow server to continue emitting subsequent chunks with a "partial_repair" attempt; hard errors must stop the stream and emit finalization metadata explaining fallback applied.

Finalization marker: stream must end with a single final_json object labeled "__stream_done__" containing: status (ok|partial|failed), emitted_sequence_count, validation_summary, and suggested_retry_token. Absent this marker, clients must treat the stream as aborted after idle-timeout or connection close.

Tool/function calling contract: when server invokes a tool, it must emit a tool_call object with: tool_name, call_id (UUID), args (object), idempotency_key, call_timestamp, expected_response_schema. The client-side or infra must be able to POST the args to the tool endpoint and return a tool_result object referencing call_id.

Deterministic handoff semantics: for any given call_id, the platform guarantees at-most-once execution unless the tool_call includes explicit "allow_retries": true. If retries are allowed, the idempotency_key must be honored by the tool to deduplicate operations. Acceptance tests must demonstrate at-most-once behavior under simulated network retries.

Fallback policy: if a primary tool endpoint returns a non-retryable error (HTTP 4xx) or the runtime deems the tool unavailable, server must follow the configured fallback order (primary -> secondary -> model-local-simulate). The stream must indicate which fallback was used in the tool_result metadata and surface reason codes for observability.

Timeouts and cancellation: tools must expose per-call timeouts. On client cancel (connection close or explicit cancel event), the runtime should attempt best-effort cancellation propagation to the tool within 200ms and emit a cancellation acknowledgment chunk. Tests must show cancellation propagation and logging of orphaned call_ids.

Observability metadata: every emitted chunk and tool_call must include trace_id and sampling flags compatible with the platform tracing system. Logs and metrics must allow reconstruction of the full request->tool->response trace for postmortem and SLA analysis.

Security: tool args must never include raw customer PII unless the customer's Private deployment explicitly allows it. The runtime must redact top-level fields marked "sensitive" in acceptance testing and include an audit entry for each tool_call that records arg_hash (SHA256) and KMS key id if encryption was applied.

Backward compatibility: non-streaming clients must continue to receive a single JSON object when streaming_mode is set to full. Acceptance tests must ensure non-streaming SDKs receive identical logical payloads compared to concatenated progressive streams.

Errors & retry tokens: when a hard error occurs, server emits a suggested_retry_token encoded with deterministic retry policy and backoff hints. The token must be verifiable by the platform so that retries are idempotent up to a time-window (configurable; default 5m).
test_plan: Unit tests for chunk marker parsing and header extraction (ENG)
Integration tests simulating intermittent network with chunk loss and reordering to validate reconstruction rules (ENG + QA)
Chaos test: drop finalization marker and verify clients treat stream as aborted after idle timeout (QA)
Tool handoff test harness: inject pass/fail responses from tool endpoints to exercise fallback order and idempotency behavior (Platform infra)
Security test: run TA redaction checks on tool args and verify audit logs record arg_hash and KMS metadata (Security)
Performance test: measure tail latency impact of progressive validation on 95/99th percentiles with 10k concurrent streams (Perf)
Contract conformance: snapshot tests that compare progressive concatenated stream -> reconstructed JSON vs canonical model output (DX)
SMOKE: Non-streaming SDK must receive same logical payload as reconstructed stream output (SDK team)
Acceptance gate: all tests must pass in Staging and be reproducible from documented test harness scripts in GitHub repo link below.

decision_log: Prefer explicit chunk markers over NDJSON to support binary payloads in chunks and to make progressive partial objects explicit.
Introduce finalization marker to handle connection aborts deterministically and to allow the runtime to provide suggested_retry_token for safe retries.
Tool handoff is represented as a tool_call object in-stream rather than a separate out-of-band protocol to preserve single-trace reconstruction and simplify client SDKs.
At-most-once default execution model with opt-in allow_retries flag for tools that can safely deduplicate.
risks: Partial JSON modes increase SDK parsing complexity; we must provide official SDK helpers to parse progressive streams.
Validation in the hot path may increase tail latency; mitigation is to provide progressive/async validation and a low-latency fast-path.
Tool idempotency depends on third-party endpoints honoring idempotency_key; fallback to model-local-simulate raises accuracy concerns.
Schema churn could lead to frequent compatibility hints; we must centralize schema release cadence in Console.
